culture.title: Drive the Midcentury Streets of Vista Las Palmas
culture.description: A few residential blocks holding more famous modernist houses than most countries, including the Kaufmann House and the House of Tomorrow.
culture.bonus: Find a butterfly roof and a breeze-block screen wall on the same street.

culture.title: Visit the Agua Caliente Cultural Plaza
culture.description: The tribe's own downtown museum, gathering plaza and bathhouse built over the hot mineral spring that the city is literally named after.
culture.bonus: Leave able to explain, in your own words, why the spring matters.

culture.title: Stand Under Albert Frey's Tramway Gas Station
culture.description: The wedge-roofed 1965 canopy at the north entrance to the city is the most photographed piece of desert modernism there is, and now the visitor centre.
culture.bonus: Get the photo from directly underneath the point of the wedge.

culture.title: Tour Cabot's Pueblo Museum
culture.description: A four-storey, 35-room Hopi-inspired pueblo that Cabot Yerxa built by hand from salvaged desert material over twenty years, with no two windows the same.
culture.bonus: Count how many windows you can find that match. The answer should be none.

culture.title: Book the Historic House Tour at Sunnylands
culture.description: Ninety minutes inside the Annenbergs' 25,000-square-foot A. Quincy Jones house, where eight presidents stayed and the art on the walls is real.
culture.bonus: Ask the guide which room the most consequential conversation happened in.

culture.title: Walk the Noah Purifoy Desert Art Museum
culture.description: Ten acres of Joshua Tree scrub holding a hundred large assemblage sculptures Purifoy built from junk in the last fifteen years of his life, free, dawn to dusk.
culture.bonus: Walk the entire ten acres without checking your phone.

culture.title: Walk the Hangars at the Palm Springs Air Museum
culture.description: One of the largest collections of flyable WWII aircraft anywhere, in open hangars where the volunteers are often the people who flew them.
culture.bonus: Get a veteran or volunteer to tell you one story about one aircraft.

culture.title: See an Exhibition at the Architecture and Design Center
culture.description: E. Stewart Williams' 1961 glass-and-steel bank building, now the art museum's design wing, where the architecture is as good as whatever is hanging in it.
culture.bonus: Work out which way the building is oriented and why, before you read a label.

social.title: See a Show at the Purple Room Supper Club
social.description: The Rat Pack's old room inside Club Trinidad, still running dinner-and-a-show cabaret with a late menu until two on weekends.
social.bonus: Book the dinner seating rather than show-only and order a Manhattan.

social.title: Catch a Drag Show at Toucans Tiki Lounge
social.description: Palm Springs' longest continuously running drag show, five nights a week in a tiki room on North Palm Canyon with a packed dance floor after.
social.bonus: Stay for the dance floor after the last number.

social.title: Drive Out to Pappy & Harriet's in Pioneertown
social.description: A cantina on a 1940s film-set street in the high desert where Paul McCartney and Robert Plant have both played to a few hundred people.
social.bonus: Stay for the whole set and eat the ribs before it starts.

social.title: Take a Table on the Arenas Strip at Chill Bar
social.description: Open 11am to 2am every day, right over the Arenas Road strip, which is the best people-watching in the Coachella Valley.
social.bonus: Get a seat facing the street and stay through the change from day to night crowd.

social.title: Take Sunset at the High Bar
social.description: Seven floors up at the Kimpton Rowan, the only rooftop pool bar in Palm Springs, with the San Jacintos filling the whole western view.
social.bonus: Be in a seat facing the mountain before the sun touches the ridge.

social.title: Do a Day of Coachella at the Empire Polo Club
social.description: Two April weekends when a polo field in Indio becomes the most photographed festival on earth, with art installations the size of buildings.
social.bonus: See one act you have never heard of all the way through, start to finish.

social.title: Order a Pu-Pu Platter at Tonga Hut
social.description: The Palm Springs branch of LA's oldest tiki bar, doing Polynesian-Cantonese food in the Hideaway out back and flaming drinks up front.
social.bonus: Order the platter that arrives on fire and share it with the table.

social.title: Watch the Firebirds at Acrisure Arena
social.description: The Seattle Kraken's AHL affiliate plays 36 home games a year in a new 10,000-seat arena, and the desert has taken to hockey harder than anyone expected.
social.bonus: Throw something on the ice at the appropriate moment, and only then.

social.title: Find Seymour's Behind Mr. Lyons
social.description: A hidden speakeasy inside the steakhouse: antique velvet, a black-and-white television and cocktails made by people who take it seriously.
social.bonus: Get in without asking anyone at the front desk where it is.

social.title: Work Through the List at Truss & Twine
social.description: A cocktail bar in the 1926 El Paseo building whose menu is arranged as a history of American drinking, open seven nights until half twelve.
social.bonus: Order the oldest drink on the menu.

social.title: Do Thursday Night VillageFest
social.description: Every Thursday the city closes Palm Canyon Drive and fills it with two hundred stalls of art, food and oddities until ten at night.
social.bonus: Eat dinner entirely from street stalls and buy one thing from an artist.

social.title: Drink Rum in the Dark at Bootlegger Tiki
social.description: A tiny red-lit tiki room in the original 1953 Don the Beachcomber space, pouring properly made tropical drinks with house syrups.
social.bonus: Order the strongest thing on the menu and share it with one other person.

8ball.title: Palm Canyon Dice Roll
8ball.description: Start at the south end of Palm Canyon Drive, roll a die, walk that many doors north and go into whatever it is. Repeat three times.
8ball.bonus: Order the house special at every stop, whatever it turns out to be.

8ball.title: Butterfly Roof Bingo
8ball.description: Pick a neighbourhood at random, then drive or ride it until you have found a butterfly roof, a breeze-block wall, a kidney pool and a pink door.
8ball.bonus: Do not use a map or a guide — only what you can see from the street.

foodie.title: Have Dinner at Workshop Kitchen + Bar
foodie.description: A James Beard design award winner inside a 1926 landmark on Palm Canyon, with concrete booths, a 25-foot bar and Michelin-recommended cooking.
foodie.bonus: Sit at the bar and have the bartender build you something not on the list.

foodie.title: Brunch on El Paseo at Wilma & Frieda
foodie.description: Comfort food with a twist on Palm Desert's smart shopping street, open 8am to 2pm daily and busy for good reason.
foodie.bonus: Order the thing your table agrees sounds the most ridiculous.

foodie.title: Order the Bacon Flight at Cheeky's
foodie.description: A Michelin-listed Palm Canyon breakfast room whose menu changes weekly and whose six-strip bacon flight is the reason for the queue on the sidewalk.
foodie.bonus: Rank all six bacons out loud and defend your winner.

foodie.title: Drink a Date Shake at Shields Date Garden
foodie.description: Since 1924, a working seventeen-acre date farm in Indio with a turquoise soda fountain that has been blending date crystals into shakes for a century.
foodie.bonus: Sit through the whole Romance and Sex Life of the Date film after your shake.

foodie.title: Build a Sandwich You Cannot Finish at Sherman's
foodie.description: A proper Jewish deli on Tahquitz Canyon Way, open 8am to 9pm, with a bakery case as long as the counter and portions from another era.
foodie.bonus: Order a whole sandwich instead of a half and take the rest home.

foodie.title: Get a Shake with a Doughnut on the Straw
foodie.description: Great Shakes on South Palm Canyon threads a warm mini-doughnut onto every straw, and the date shake is the one to get in this town.
foodie.bonus: Eat the doughnut before you drink any of the shake.

foodie.title: Have a Martini at Melvyn's
foodie.description: The Ingleside Estate dining room where Sinatra actually drank, still doing tableside classics with a piano going in the corner.
foodie.bonus: Order something flambeed at the table.

foodie.title: Order a Steak at Mr. Lyons
foodie.description: A reimagined 1940s chophouse on South Palm Canyon with seven separate rooms, jazz standards and martinis that arrive very cold.
foodie.bonus: Eat in a different room from the one you were first offered.

foodie.title: Queue Up at Rooster and the Pig
foodie.description: A tiny Vietnamese-American room on South Indian Canyon that takes no reservations and has been on national best-restaurant lists anyway.
foodie.bonus: Get there at opening, order four dishes for two people and finish them.

foodie.title: Eat in the Courtyard at FARM
foodie.description: A Provencal kitchen tucked into the historic La Plaza courtyard, all bougainvillea and bistro chairs, with a three-course prix fixe at dinner.
foodie.bonus: Take the prix fixe and let them choose every course.

foodie.title: Take a Patio Table at Birba
foodie.description: The sunken patio next door to Cheeky's, with hedges, string lights, a fire pit and Tuscan pizza out of the back.
foodie.bonus: Stay past the point where the string lights become the only light.

foodie.title: Take the Margarita Flight at Tac/Quila
foodie.description: A hacienda-style room on North Palm Canyon in the Michelin Guide, doing street tacos and a lobster taco with equal seriousness.
foodie.bonus: Do the margarita flight and name your favourite before the server tells you which is which.

chill.title: Walk the Cactarium at Moorten Botanical Garden
chill.description: A one-acre family garden on South Palm Canyon with 3,000 desert species and the world's first enclosed cactus greenhouse, for five dollars.
chill.bonus: Learn the name of one plant you have never heard of and remember it.

chill.title: Walk the Living Desert Zoo and Gardens
chill.description: A thousand acres in Palm Desert that is half botanical garden and half desert-species zoo, with giraffes you can feed by hand.
chill.bonus: Feed the giraffes and get the photo.

chill.title: Shop the Uptown Design District
chill.description: Six blocks of North Palm Canyon full of midcentury furniture dealers, vintage racks and design bookshops that are genuinely worth the browse.
chill.bonus: Buy one thing under twenty dollars that you will actually keep.

chill.title: Soak the Mineral Waters at Two Bunch Palms
chill.description: An adults-only wellness resort in Desert Hot Springs built on natural hot mineral springs, with a grotto, mud treatments and a no-phones policy by the water.
chill.bonus: Do the full mud wrap, however undignified it feels.

chill.title: Take a Pool Day at the Ace Hotel & Swim Club
chill.description: The converted motor lodge on East Palm Canyon that set the template for the Palm Springs pool day, with a DJ, a spa and King's Highway for lunch.
chill.bonus: Stay in or beside the water for three uninterrupted hours.

chill.title: Wander the Gardens at Sunnylands Center
chill.description: Fifteen acres of desert gardens and a walking labyrinth around the Annenberg estate's visitor centre, free to enter and almost silent.
chill.bonus: Walk the full labyrinth without cutting a corner.

chill.title: Stargaze at Sky's The Limit Observatory
chill.description: A volunteer-run observatory and nature centre outside Joshua Tree's north entrance that opens its telescopes to the public on star party nights.
chill.bonus: Look at one thing through the big telescope that you could not name beforehand.

chill.title: Start the Day at Ernest Coffee
chill.description: Stumptown coffee and local pastries in the same building where Don the Beachcomber opened his tiki restaurant in 1953, open from 6am.
chill.bonus: Get there before seven and take the outside table.

chill.title: Spend an Afternoon in the Palm Springs Art Museum
chill.description: A serious modern and Western art collection in an E. Stewart Williams building right under the mountain, with a sculpture garden out back.
chill.bonus: Find the Chihuly and sit with it for five minutes.

chill.title: Swim Laps at the Palm Springs Swim Center
chill.description: A city-run Olympic-size outdoor pool in Sunrise Park, heated year round, where locals swim under the mountain for a few dollars.
chill.bonus: Swim a full kilometre without stopping at the wall.

adventure.title: Snowshoe Long Valley Straight Off the Tram
adventure.description: In winter you can leave a 75-degree desert, ride ten minutes uphill and strap on snowshoes in a silent pine basin under snow.
adventure.bonus: Send someone a photo of the snow without telling them where you are.

adventure.title: Hike Devil's Slide to Suicide Rock in Idyllwild
adventure.description: An hour up the mountain from the desert floor, a granite-slab summit in real alpine forest where it is twenty-five degrees cooler.
adventure.bonus: Eat lunch sitting on the bare slab with your legs over the edge.

adventure.title: Drive to Salvation Mountain and the Salton Sea
adventure.description: Ninety minutes south is a shrinking inland sea with beaches made of fish bones and, beside it, a hand-painted adobe mountain built by one man over thirty years.
adventure.bonus: Climb the yellow brick road to the top of Salvation Mountain.

adventure.title: Do Hidden Valley and Barker Dam in Joshua Tree
adventure.description: Two short loops that show you everything Joshua Tree is good at: house-sized boulder piles, a hidden cattle-rustler's basin and petroglyphs by a desert reservoir.
adventure.bonus: Scramble to the top of one boulder pile with no trail on it.

adventure.title: Find the Ladders in Painted Canyon
adventure.description: A slot-canyon loop in the Mecca Hills where you climb bolted metal ladders out of a crack in the earth and walk a ridgeline back down.
adventure.bonus: Go up every ladder without using your knees on the rungs.

adventure.title: Hike Tahquitz Canyon to the Waterfall
adventure.description: A two-mile Agua Caliente loop into a canyon behind downtown that ends at a 60-foot waterfall running out of bare rock.
adventure.bonus: Stand close enough to the falls to get properly wet.

adventure.title: Take an E-Bike Around Palm Springs
adventure.description: The valley is flat, the streets are wide and Bike Palm Springs will hand you a RAD electric cruiser and a map of the good neighbourhoods.
adventure.bonus: Ride every street in Vista Las Palmas before you return the bike.

adventure.title: Walk Palm Canyon in the Indian Canyons
adventure.description: The largest California fan palm oasis in the world, fifteen miles of it, on Agua Caliente land just south of the city.
adventure.bonus: Get far enough in that you cannot hear another person.

adventure.title: Rope Up with Cliffhanger Guides in Joshua Tree
adventure.description: Joshua Tree is one of the great climbing areas on earth, and Cliffhanger's certified guides will put a first-timer on real granite for a full day.
adventure.bonus: Lead or top out one route that scared you when you looked up at it.

adventure.title: Play a Twilight Round at Indian Canyons Golf Resort
adventure.description: Late-afternoon rates on a classic desert course with the San Jacintos going pink behind every green.
adventure.bonus: Finish the round before the light goes, even if it means running the last hole.

adventure.title: Ride the Aerial Tramway to Mount San Jacinto
adventure.description: The world's largest rotating tramcar lifts you from the desert floor to 8,516 feet in ten minutes, dropping the temperature thirty degrees and putting you in pine forest.
adventure.bonus: Hike at least a mile into Long Valley before you get back on the tram.

adventure.title: Take the Red Jeep Tour Into the San Andreas Fault
adventure.description: Desert Adventures runs open-air Jeeps onto a private ranch in the Indio Hills and walks you down into the actual fault zone with a naturalist.
adventure.bonus: Put a hand on each side of the fault at the same time.

adventure.title: Climb the Bump and Grind Trail
adventure.description: Palm Desert's cardio pilgrimage: a relentless switchbacked climb that every local has an opinion about, with the whole valley behind you at the top.
adventure.bonus: Do the full climb without stopping to rest.

adventure.title: Go Up at Sunrise with Fantasy Balloon Flights
adventure.description: Launching from the date groves at first light, drifting over the Coachella Valley in silence, and landing to champagne.
adventure.bonus: Help the crew pack the envelope after you land.

adventure.title: Walk the Boardwalk at Thousand Palms Oasis
adventure.description: The Coachella Valley Preserve sits directly on the San Andreas Fault, where groundwater forced to the surface grows a palm jungle in open desert.
adventure.bonus: Walk the McCallum Trail all the way to the pond at the end.

adventure.title: Watch the Sun Set from Keys View
adventure.description: A five-thousand-foot overlook where the San Andreas Fault, the Salton Sea and the whole Coachella Valley lie out below you as the light goes orange.
adventure.bonus: Stay until the valley lights come on and you can pick out Palm Springs.
